scrutiny.test: T0 purpose: prismis runs unattended on a small host (constitution: local-first, zero-ops); a client request that can OOM the daemon is the #55 outage class, and this closes it for every client, not only updated ones.
scrutiny.failureCase: A fix that still depends on every client being current.

scrutiny.test: T1 owners: get_content_list owns the bounded read (storage.py:944) and the per-item helpers own the mirrored fields; the stream reuses both rather than re-deriving them.
scrutiny.failureCase: A second list query or a second field computation.

scrutiny.test: T2 same noun: the 2,954 / 642 / 2,176 MB figures were measured through the real app on a copy of cerebro's real database, and the trigger request was read from cerebro's observability log for the window with the 2.9 GB peak.
T3 degrade: a mid-stream database error truncates the body instead of returning a 500, and responses lose Content-Length; both stated.
T6 assumption checked: FastAPI 0.142.3 keeps request-scoped yield dependencies open until the response is sent (fastapi/routing.py request_response), so get_storage's connection outlives the stream.
scrutiny.failureCase: A stream reading from a closed connection.

scrutiny.test: T7 consumers: /api/entries is read by the TUI (limit=10000, view=list), the web UI (limit 100), the CLI's list (<=100) and export (<=1000), and old TUIs (limit=10000, full); the body shape stays identical for all, proven by an equality test.
scrutiny.failureCase: A client that parses a changed body.

scrutiny.test: T11 class, every GET endpoint in api.py: /api/entries (unbounded up to 10,000, streamed here), /api/search (le=50), /api/entries/{id} and /raw (one item), kinds, prune count, archive status, statistics, health (small); the middleware's body buffering is removed for all of them.
scrutiny.failureCase: Another unbounded body left in memory.

scrutiny.test: T13 two places: get_content_list becomes list(iter_content_list(...)) so the SQL lives once.
scrutiny.failureCase: Two copies of the list query.

scrutiny.test: T20 walk: bishop's old TUI sends limit=10000 with no view; the handler validates, opens the stream, writes items one at a time from the cursor, logs item_count from request.state when done; RSS stays near the slim request's; the old TUI parses the same envelope it always did.
scrutiny.failureCase: A step where the full list is materialized.

decisions.question: Harden the daemon against old full-list clients, or rely on updating every TUI?
decisions.answer: Update bishop and harden the daemon (operator, 2026-10-10).
